explanation: A search-tree node can cache how many tracked occurrences lie in its left subtree. Route equal inserted values left, so that count also includes earlier/later duplicates beneath an equal node. A rank query accumulates entire left subtrees and ancestor nodes only when moving right; finding the queried value adds its left count without counting that node itself.
correctness: Every insertion preserves the BST rule left<=node<right and increments a node's left count exactly when the new occurrence enters that left subtree. During a query, the accumulated count contains exactly the smaller/equal occurrences already skipped on right turns. At equality, every left-subtree occurrence is <=value, and the current node is the one excluded occurrence, so accumulated+leftCount is the required rank. If traversal reaches no matching node, the value is absent and -1 is returned regardless of the partial accumulated count. Iterative traversal avoids recursion-depth failures on a skewed stream.
walkthrough: Track 5,1,4,4. Sorted tracked values are [1,4,4,5]. GetRank(4) returns 2: one 1 and the OTHER 4 count, while one queried 4 is excluded. GetRank(2) returns -1 even though its insertion position would be 1. A new tracker begins empty.
timeComplexity: O(h) per Track/GetRank for tree height h. The actual BST is not balanced: worst-case h equals the number of tracked occurrences; do not claim guaranteed logarithmic time.
spaceComplexity: O(t) stored nodes after t tracked occurrences and O(1) auxiliary iterative traversal space, excluding the returned transcript results.
edgeCases: Query before any Track and query an absent interior value.
Repeated equal values count other copies; negative and signed-endpoint values.
Ascending/descending streams create skewed trees but not recursive stack overflow.
